case_name: Sher-E-Kashmir Institute Of Medical vs M/S Siemens Pvt. Ltd

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Soura, Srinagar (through its Director)
parties.respondent_defendant: M/S Siemens Pvt. Ltd (through Mr. Rahul Sharma, Advocate)

facts_of_case: Petitioner invited offers for supply/installation/testing of three medical equipment; respondent submitted bids and they were accepted; petitioner released payment for the supplied equipment.

legal_principles.principle: An award can be set aside if it is contrary to the fundamental policy of Indian law, the interest of India, or justice or morality, or if it is patently illegal.
legal_principles.held: Even prior to the incorporation of amendments in terms of the Act of 3 of 2016 in Section 34 of the Act of 1996, it was held by the Supreme Court that an award could be set aside if it is contrary to the fundamental policy of Indian law, the interest of India, or justice or morality, or if it is patently illegal.

legal_principles.principle: The expressions 'public policy of State/India' would embrace within their purview the expressions 'fundamental policy of India law', 'interest of India', 'justice or morality' and 'patent illegality'.
legal_principles.held: Thus, non-incorporation of the amendments made vide Act No. 03 of 2016 to the Act of 1996 in the Act of 1997, which governs the present case, would not make any difference to the scope and power of this Court to interfere in the impugned award passed by Arb P No.18/2023 c/w the learned Arbitrator.

outcome.final_order: Three petitions under Section 34 of the Jammu and Kashmir Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1997 are allowed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for challenging an arbitration award
assisting in a contract dispute involving supply and installation of equipment
advising on the tender process for government projects
